newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Bolivia's Vinto tin smelter on strike - union.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia's Vinto tin smelter on strike - union.

text.p: Workers at Bolivia's Vinto tin smelter have launched an indefinite strike after the soon-to-be-privatized company issued employment termination papers to more than half its workforce, a union leader said.
"They launched their protest on Monday," Bolivia's labor federation (COB) secretary general, Eduardo Calderon told Reuters.
Vinto officials were not available for comment.
Calderon said more than 500 of the approximately 1,000 workers received their notice to quit on Monday.
The Bolivian Miners Federation, part of COB, added that some 500 workers at the Colquiri and Huanuni tin mines were also on strike.
Vinto, whose full title is Empresas Metalurgica Vinto, has a production capacity of 24,000 to 25,000 tonnes per year of low lead tin.
This year's production was forecast, before the strike, to be almost 18,000 tonnes. The smelter also produces some 4,500 to 5,000 tonnes per year of antimony.
Vinto is slated for privatisation in January but has recently been plagued by a series of protests and stoppages because of workforce opposition to the privatisation.
The privatisation has been delayed several times because the two mines, which supplies some of Vinto's feed, protested against the selloff.

Four companies have been short-listed in the privatisation process. They are: Glencore International of Switzerland, Australia's Renison Goldfields Consolidated, Smelting Corp Berhad of Malaysia, and Brazil's Paranapanema.
Peru's Minsur tin mining and smelting company also supplies tin concentrates for tolling into metal at Vinto.
